steps.text: Place ribs, 2 onions cut into wedges, 4 tablespoons soy sauce, star anise pods, and black pepper in a large stock pot . Add water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium low, cover, and simmer until ribs are tender when pierced, about 1 ¼ hours, stirring occasionally.

Meanwhile, heat oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add 1 onion chopped; cook and stir until onion is soft. Stir in honey, brown sugar, remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce, ginger, Worcestershire sauce, and lemon juice; cook and stir until well blended. Remove from heat.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Remove ribs from stock pot using tongs; arrange in a single layer in an 11x16-inch baking pan. Brush evenly with honey glaze.
Bake in the preheated oven, basting often with pan drippings, until ribs are well glazed, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Filipino Ribs
raw_recipe.description: This Filipino ribs recipe simmers ribs in soy sauce, onions, and star anise, then finishes with a honey, ginger, lemon, soy Worcestershire sauce glaze.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was great. Sweet, but not artificial tasting. Unfortunately, the recipe omits what kind of liquid to "bring to a boil". Pretty sure it's not the 4T of soy sauce. I just used a couple cups of water and it was fine. I also wished they described the consistency of the honey sauce to know when it is done. I tried to reduce it some and let it simmer only about 5 minutes.

I am filipino and I like it sweet. Here are my changes. 

1 - I buy baby back ribs or back ribs. The ones that are smaller. I usually do about 3 pounds. If you want leftovers, I would do more. I also use a big stock pot for this.
2 - I use sweet onions. 
3 - I also use sweet soy sauce. I usually use like half a cup of the sauce in the pot mixture and when I make the glaze I also use another half cup of sweet soy sauce.
4 - It doesn't tell you to add liquid to boil the ribs in. I usually add enough beef stock to cover the the ribs along with all the ingredients that it tells you to put into the pot. When the ribs meat start to flake when you put a fork in it then you are done.
5- I use white pepper instead of black pepper. I find that it isn't so strong. 
6 - I find that the glaze is too little so I usually double it because after I take it out of the pot and put it on the cookie sheet which I wrap in foil. (Make it easier on yourself so that when you are done cooking you can just pull up the foil and toss it out). I baste the ribs good and cover with foil. In the last 10-15 mins of cooking, I take the foil off and baste it again. 
7 - Also when making the sauce, taste it. If it's too sweet cut back on the soy sauce. Also you can add some rice vinegar to ease off some of the sweetness. I usually make the sauce in the last 20 mins before the meat is done.

I followed the advice of several reviews - used 3.5 lbs ribs but did not reduce the other ingredients. I used 1/2 cup water, 6 tablespoons soy sauce and 4 1/2 pods of star anis to boil the ribs in a slow cooker for 6 hours. I added 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes to the sauce. The heat from the pepper flakes definitely makes a difference. The sauce turned out to be sweet and tangy with a kick.

These ribs were fabulous! Made with 3 pounds of ribs and did everything else as written. I did incorporate a few suggestions though. Added 1/2 c. water to braising pot. Added 1/4 c. braising liquid to sauce. Added 1/4 tsp. red pepper flakes to sauce. Everything was so easy and delicious. Had just the right amount of sauce--only 1 Tbs. left when they were done. While I was waiting for the oven to preheat, I just set the ribs, meat side down, in the pan of sauce and let them soak (I also basted several times) while the oven heated. Then, basted every 8 minutes for a total of 32 minutes cooking time in the oven. Beautiful mahogany color, tender yet still with a little chew. For us, this was dinner for two; it was a half a slab each and we thoroughly enjoyed. Three pounds probably amounts to 4 regular servings. I'll be sharing this recipe with lots of family and friends. They're gonna love it! Oh, yeah. I saved the braising liquid and onions and I think I'll make a pot of rice with it. We'll see. Too good to toss. Don't forget to line your pan with foil--you'll be sorry if you don't.

I struggle with ribs. Cooking. Method, tenderness, flavour

Having read reviews I made a number of changes

I did precook the ribs as directed. No additional liquid. The flavours were great. 1 1/2 h was enough for tender to fork

The sauce I made a number of changes. I doubled the amount of sauce to begin with. I started w 3 c of onions and cooked in butter with a lid on a large sauce pan for 25 minutes, in the manner of Indian precooking. This reduced the onions almost to a paste. Then I added the remaining ingredients but halved the honey, increased the lemon juice, added 1 tsp of chilli flakes, and I tsp of cumin to layer the flavours. 

I drained the ribs, and cooked over medium low barbecue for 20 min to char and basted w the glaze severAl times. 

Turned out really well. Will make again

Final note - kept and defatted the juices after the precooking. - will make great stock

Excellent taste and very easy to make. I did use my slow cooker and cooked the ribs for roughly 8 hours on low. Had to add an additional 1 cup liquid (you can use either water or broth). Absolutely agree with other raters that you have to at least triple the sauce for basting. The only changes I made were to cut back on the Honey & Brown Sugar after reading some of the reviews - didn't want it to be too sweet. Got Rave reviews from my dinner guest - Two Thumbs Up!

We loved it. I added 1/2 cup of vegetable broth to cooking mixture, and braised instead of boiled the ribs in a Dutch oven. Added liquid from cooking to BBQ sauce, along with a pinch more ginger and garlic.

Instead of boiling ribs, I wrapped them in aluminum foil with the onions, soy sauce, pepper and star anise (I used 2 not 6). I baked them in a 350 degree oven for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours. I removed them from the foil, increased the oven to 400 degrees laid the ribs in the baking sheet and basted them as directed. I have been using this method for all my ribs for a long time and they are always fall-off-bone tender and very flavorful

I give this 4 stars as written, but it definitely is 5 stars with my revisions! First thing, I boiled the ribs w/ an extra 1/2c water and I added about 1/4c of that liquid from boiling the ribs and added it to the sauce; it gave it good extra flavor. Also, definitely double the sauce! The sauce has wonderful flavor and if you made it as written, it's not enough to cover the ribs fully. Secondly, I used fennel instead of the star anise because that's what I had and it does make for a good substitute. Thirdly, I used only 1/4c honey and I think if I used the full 1/2c it would have come out way too sweet. The ribs itself also came out very tender and juicy! I think I will always cook my ribs this way regardless of what sauce I use on them!

First I didn't boil the meat. 

Second, it was too hot out to use the oven so I ended up grilling them. Brushed the ribs with olive oil and put them on indirect heat on the grill for 30 minutes on each side while maintaining a grill temp between 350 and 400. Then I turned them again and brushed the top with the glaze and turned them every 5-10 minutes for 35 minutes brushing the top with the glaze each time I turned them. It's Important to to keep them over the Indirect heat with all the honey in the sauce or they will burn really quickly. 

These were delicious and are a keeper. Better yet it doesn't heat up the kitchen on a hot day.
Very easy to make, good flavor, and pretty tender! It's a fast and easy recipe to make ribs and definitely takes Filipino.

My wife wrote on the recipe,"Best Ribs Ever!" She is not a rib eater as she does not like to get her hands messy, but she said these were worth it as they tasted wonderful. I struggled with how much water to add in the beginning as I have par-boiled ribs in the past to get that "wet" effect you find in some restaurants. I added 1/2 cup water, and with the onions and ribs themselves it added enough moisture so that after the initial pot steam stage there was plenty of liquid at the bottom of the pot. Hated to throw it out. The glaze worked perfectly too, so worth the effort, which was really not that much. Great use of star anise that can sit in your spice cupboard for ever if you don't find some way to employ it into a recipe. Thanks for this great recipe.

I love this recipe! A bit time consuming, but not difficult. Perfectly fun recipe now that I’m Covid-working from home. Did not have star anise on hand, but was still delicious! Kids and hubby loved it too.
This is an amazing recipe! Makes the perfect cornbread!
I used Two star anise, thumbs up.
Sweet and fall off the bone great.

I did like them but I would use only 2 star anise for the flavor to me was overly powerful. I can see that the next I will like them a lot better though! Will make them again with less star anise and know the family would like them.

Usually I read reviews first, but didn't this time- slight mistake. I cut the recipe in half and followed it exactly, inculuding NOT adding extra liquid (broth or water) when boiling the ribs. They still came out moist and tasty. It's time consuming, but easy. The ribs are way too sweet for me, but flavorful and delicious otherwise.
Love it ..!
